metric.counted_paths: Every changed repository path in git diff --no-renames upstream_commit..target except an explicit non-production exclusion or a new project-owned addition. Each remaining path must be assigned to exactly one bridge group.
metric.counted_lines: The additions and deletions reported by git diff --no-renames --numstat upstream_commit..target for counted paths, including production source, base resources, schemas, manifests, and other non-excluded upstream/bridge paths.
metric.classification_precedence: An explicit bridge-group path is counted before every exclusion, so an organizer-owned localized resource remains visible. Next a content-pinned known non-production change is excluded only while both sides still match the recorded upstream and target Git blobs, so an upstream rebase that alters either side fails closed for ownership review. Structural explicit exclusions follow, then explicit exclusion precedes project-owned addition.
metric.pinned_exclusion_rule: Production-capable paths such as build configuration files and localized resource directories are never excluded by pattern alone. A pinned path is excluded only at its recorded upstream AND target content pair; a candidate whose upstream blob, target blob, or both diverge fails the measurement and requires Issue-owned review before the pin is refreshed or the path joins a bridge group.
metric.binary_paths: Git binary numstat records are retained through classification. An explicitly excluded binary contributes one excluded file and zero line counts; a binary path that would be counted fails the measurement.
metric.comparison_rule: Growth is a positive delta in counted files, additions, or deletions. It requires review and an Issue-owned rationale; it is not a quality score or an automatic regression verdict.

exclusions: Documentation, specifications, assessments, workflows, repository-contract tooling, test sources, test-only build configuration, generated files, and vendored files are not production upstream patch surface.
New production modules under project_owned_addition_prefixes are reported separately and do not enter the counted metric.
Base resources, schemas, manifests, and every other non-excluded path must be assigned to an explicit bridge group before the measurement can pass.

Known pure translation churn under localized values-* directories is pinned to its recorded upstream/target content pair instead of being excluded by locale-directory prefix; a new localized production change therefore returns to ownership review.

Extensions, build paths, and localized resource directories that could carry a production change (images, YAML configuration, build.gradle, dependency catalogs, values-*/strings.xml) are never excluded by pattern alone. Known non-production changes to such paths are pinned to their exact recorded content pair and fail closed on divergence.

Binary font assets retained from the 15-era fork (lawnchair/res/font/inter_*.ttf; upstream 16 replaced Inter with Google Sans Flex) cannot carry a text line metric; they are excluded as explicit paths at this candidate and require ownership review (pin conversion or deletion) at formal baseline adoption.

build.gradle.reason: Root Gradle build script differs from upstream only in test-only and tooling-only build configuration at this baseline; any further edit requires ownership review.

gradle/libs.versions.toml.reason: Version catalog changes at this baseline are consumed by project-owned organizer tooling and tests only; any further edit requires ownership review per AGENTS.md dependency policy.

bridge_groups.responsibility: Retire the historical Deck runtime and normalize its bounded artifacts without restoring a historical layout.
Expose manual organizer, category override, and placement-lock controls through Lawnchair UI seams.
Bridge organizer writes, model reload, and serialized layout mutation through minimal Launcher3 ownership seams.
Preserve organizer lock state and recovery invariants across Launcher database schema, restore, and migration paths.

Visual multi-select edit surface (Issue #449, ADR-0014 case B): pure session/planning layers, thin organizer-access window, full-screen UI, and the two entries. Since Issue #452 this file also hosts the fork's added popup entries generally (organize_home for #452, alongside edit_surface for #449) plus the DEFAULT_ORDER-relative order restoration and the no-op write guard; #452's share of this file's growth is adopted with #452 rationale. The one-shot apply goes through the existing organizer apply path (ORGANIZER lease, one recovery point, 1 transaction, correlated reload + verification); no direct DB writes. Includes the plan-coupled minimal extension of the apply path: the manifest-absence delete pass in LauncherLayoutAdapter (plan 結合点7) that materializes intended-row removals, and the read-only inspectCapture seam in LayoutApplicationModule. Since Issue #507 it also hosts the duplicate-group projection (EditSurfaceDuplicateGroups) over the session-applied working diagram; the #451 detection rule is generalized in place (planning/DuplicateLaunchTargets.kt, behavior-invariant delegation) and the last-one guard runs only at the duplicate-dialog boundaries. Since Issue #508 the shared read-only diagram parts (page surface, cell placement, item visuals) extracted from EditSurfaceScreen live in ui/diagram/HomeDiagramParts.kt and are counted here; the organizer confirmation's before/after diagrams consume the same parts (#508 rationale: minimal extraction, no selection/session/icon logic shared).

Edit undo (Issue #450, ADR-0013 contract 5): the generation-bound process-local undo record, the pure undo planner with availability verification, the undo executor and snackbar entry, and the recovery-result text mapper. The inverse operations themselves live in ModelWriter via the DirectEditContract extension (already in the direct-edit bridge group); the edit-session undo reuses the existing organizer recovery path through the HomeEditSurfaceAccess window (receipt accessor additive to ManualOrganizationApplication). Also owns the one upstream bind-path guard created for this Issue: Folder.java suppresses the bind-time single-child cleanup for a folder carrying the direct-edit OPTIONS bit, so the cleanup cannot flatten it inside the undo snackbar's window.

Organizer run entry from the workspace long-press popup (Issue #452): the popup edit screen's locked-state branch, the entry's monochrome icon, and the order-restoration contract are owned here. The organize_home OptionItem/DEFAULT_ORDER entry itself lives in the fork's shared options-popup entries file (LauncherOptionsPopup.kt, counted under homeedit-edit-surface because #449 first patched that file); its growth is adopted with #452 rationale. No model, loader, or DB path: the handler only opens PreferenceActivity at the HomeScreenManualOrganization route.

Pre-existing fork platform changes that predate Issue #449 and are already in the baseline upstream..main diff (backup/restore UI, bugreport, device-profile config, build configuration). Recorded for measurement completeness; ownership review of each belongs to the issues that introduced them.

New-app destination policy (Issue #497, ADR-0015; category mode added by Issue #594 / ADR-0017): the pure planner with the closed result, the snapshot classifier, the category-mode pure resolution + mapping codec + capture decision seam (AppDestinationCategoryResolver.kt, incl. CategoryModeCapture), the capture-time signal reader reusing the organizer sources (CategoryModeSignalReader.kt), the settings row + folder picker + category mapping editor wiring, and the minimal upstream writer surface (AddWorkspaceItemsTask / ItemInstallQueue / PersistedItemArray) that realizes the ADR-0013 contract 4 admission-in-completion write. Registered here retroactively: the paths were merged with PR #498 but the bridge assignment missing from this inventory was only surfaced by the Issue #507 measurement.
